origin.description: Truncate long strings and pad them to a field width.
origin.usage: utf8_format(x, trim = FALSE, chars = NULL, justify = "left", width = NULL, na.encode = TRUE, quote = FALSE, na.print = NULL, print.gap = NULL, utf8 = NULL)

arguments.name: chars
arguments.text: Display units to keep before the ellipsis.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Minimum field width. NULL pads to the longest element.

arguments.name: utf8
arguments.text: Use a UTF-8 ellipsis. When false, non-ASCII is escaped first.

origin.details: Wide characters count as two units. The ellipsis is extra, not part of the budget.

translation.description: The ellipsis is U+2026 when the locale is UTF-8. Right alignment keeps the suffix.
translation.usage: utf8_format(x, trim=False, chars=None, justify="left", width=None, na_encode=True, quote=False, na_print=None, print_gap=None, utf8=None)

arguments.name: chars
arguments.text: Display units to keep before the ellipsis.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Minimum field width. NULL pads to the longest element.

arguments.name: utf8
arguments.text: Use a UTF-8 ellipsis. When false, non-ASCII is escaped first.

translation.details: na_encode, na_print, and print_gap are the R na.encode, na.print, and print.gap names.
translation.example:
from utf8 import utf8_format
print(utf8_format("fa\u00e7ile", chars=3))
